answer: Forging 363 aliases thus costs 461 bonds held for 14 days each, plus the bridge attestations those aliases can never earn. Each identity must lock a bond, called an inlet, before it can post or attest. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. A single crystal checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
